claims.text: Data-driven machine-learning optimization of multi-step annealing and quenching cycles can improve control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Improved control of nucleation and growth kinetics produces tailored phase assemblages.
As-cast or conventionally processed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs exhibit a heterogeneous mixture of phases.
The heterogeneous phase mixture in these alloys is caused by uncontrolled phase transformations.
A predictive machine-learning model can optimize the temperature profiles, dwell times, and cooling rates of multi-step annealing and quenching cycles.
Control of nucleation events and growth kinetics mediates the formation and distribution of constituent phases.
The predictive model uses existing experimental data to tune thermal-cycle parameters.
Tuning thermal-cycle parameters with the model precisely adjusts nucleation and growth kinetics.
Selective kinetic control promotes a more uniform phase assemblage.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will produce a refined microstructure with a more uniform and predictable phase distribution.
The refined and more uniform phase distribution will enhance the mechanical properties of the alloy.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will yield more reproducible mechanical properties than conventional processing.
Traditional annealing and quenching without model optimization results in uncontrolled phase distributions.
Traditional annealing and quenching produces inconsistent microstructural outcomes.
The method may be less effective under extreme processing conditions.
Sparse training data in a composition range may limit the method's effectiveness in that range.
The method's applicability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the model's training data.
Model accuracy and the representativeness of training data introduce uncertainty into the proposed method.
Transferability of the proposed method across experimental setups remains to be validated.
